title: STILL PRESENT (r3): the wrong-person leg's taken-over stand-down is read-time only — apply_wrong_person still executes the unguarded update_reference_call_status, so a take-over between the token read and the UPDATE still yanks a landlord-handled row into awaiting_correction (TOCTOU)
evidence:
form_handler.gleam:1235: `case row.taken_over_at != "" {` ... 1249-1257: `case
                sql.update_reference_call_status(
                  config.db,
                  id_uuid,
                  sql.AwaitingCorrection,
                  "",
                  "contact_invalid",
                  sql.ContactInitiated,
                )`; update_reference_call_status.sql:23-24: `WHERE id = $1
  AND status = $5::reference_call_status
RETURNING id::text;` (no taken_over_at clause); test 1744-1747: `// The dedicated guarded UPDATE 0-rows — the row is never yanked.
  let assert Ok(returned) =
    rc_sql.mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person(db, call)` — calls the guarded SQL DIRECTLY; `grep -rn mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person server/src/` → only sql.gleam + the .sql file, no handler call site.
detail: Guarded SQL exists but never called from server/src — apply_wrong_person still runs unguarded update_reference_call_status (status-only WHERE; take-over preserves status). Pin calls guarded SQL directly (vacuous); POST test's take-over predates the read, read-time check alone passes.
recommended_fix: Wire mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person into apply_wrong_person's awaiting arm; add a POST-route race test whose take-over lands after the token read so an unwired backstop turns it red.
